tools.description: Run a Python script against the open document in ONE step: all its changes are one transaction group (all or nothing, one undo step; for agents one proposal the user accepts or rejects). Use it instead of many single tool calls. The script runs in the user's python3 with the `ferro` SDK: `doc` (ferro.Document) and `tools` (one function per Ferro tool, same names and arguments) are predefined, e.g. `walls = doc.create_walls([(0, 0), ("8m", 0), ("8m", "6m"), (0, "6m")], closed=True, height="3m")`. Set a variable `result` to return JSON data. An uncaught exception or a non-zero exit rolls everything back (ferro.python.failed, traceback in stderr); running past timeout_s kills it and rolls back (ferro.python.timeout). `with doc.transaction("name"):` makes a block all or nothing inside the script. With in_design_option the changes go into that design option, not the shared model. Returns {ok, stdout, stderr (64 KB each at most), result, changed: [element ids], failures}.

code.description: Python 3 source. `doc`, `tools` and `ferro` are predefined; lengths in mm or strings with units ("3m").

in_design_option.description: Optional design option id: every change the script makes goes into that option's layer (a call may still name its own in_design_option). In the app, defaults to the option the user is editing.

timeout_s.description: Time limit in seconds (default 30, at most 300).

tools.name: run_python
